name: Dubbelkingen
description: Dubbelkingen (Double King) is the premier Flemish variation of the European compendium game known as King. Played primarily in Belgium, it is an marathon trick-taking game consisting of 20 distinct deals. The first half of the game focuses on 'Negative' contracts where players must avoid specific cards or tricks to sidestep penalty points, while the second half switches to 'Positive' contracts where players bid and seek to win tricks. Dubbelkingen adds a strategic layer by allowing players to choose their contracts based on their hand strength, rather than following a fixed sequence.

content.text: Dubbelkingen (Double King) is the premier Flemish variation of the European compendium game known as King. Played primarily in Belgium, it is an marathon trick-taking game consisting of 20 distinct deals. The first half of the game focuses on 'Negative' contracts where players must avoid specific cards or tricks to sidestep penalty points, while the second half switches to 'Positive' contracts where players bid and seek to win tricks. Dubbelkingen adds a strategic layer by allowing players to choose their contracts based on their hand strength, rather than following a fixed sequence.

King games are popular across Europe (resembling Barbu), but the Belgian 'Kingen' developed a specific scoring system in the early 20th century. 'Dubbelkingen' was created for serious players who felt the standard 10nddeal game was too reliant on the luck of the deal.
52ndcard deck, complex score sheet for 20 deals.
Each player receives 13 cards. Dealing is usually done in batches (4-4nd5).
